name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with PVI of D+18
Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage ($7.4M raised)
Prediction markets price Democrats near 96% to hold the seat
Open seat after Crockett's retirement, but no sign of a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean, Allred's dominant fundraising, and markets pricing a Democratic hold near 96% all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat. No polling or expert ratings exist, so uncertainty stays elevated, but nothing suggests a genuine contest.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Gillespie within single digits, or signs of Democratic underfunding after Allred's cash burn, would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jasmine Crockett's retirement leaves this Dallas-area seat open, but the district remains firmly Democratic with an 18-point partisan lean. Colin Allred, a well-known former congressman and Senate nominee, enters as the heavy favorite and has raised over $7 million, dwarfing Republican Patrick Gillespie, who reports little or no fundraising activity.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the forecast leans on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic hold at roughly 96 percent. The seat is rated Safe D, with the main caveat being the usual uncertainty of an open-seat contest in a low-information race.
